verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'aching all over' and 'definitely the last six weeks' with 'feeling really tired, run down.'
When asked when last well, patient states 'definitely Christmas, New Year, I felt relatively well.'
Patient says he was on holiday in the States 'End of January, start of Feb' and that symptoms started 'probably a couple of weeks after I got back.'
Patient: 'I'm probably less hungry, but no, no weight change' and 'probably slightly smaller portions... more of an effort to actually eat everything.'

Patient describes rash 'sort of calf, back of my calf', first noticed 'around the end of February, the middle to end of Feb,' 'didn't actually cause too much itching,' and 'it faded over a couple of weeks.'
Regarding time of rash, patient says 'it turns out it was a bit of a sore throat I had... so possibly a little bit feverish,' supporting possible concurrent sore throat and fever.
Patient reports 'aching shoulders, back, the hips, knees' and denies swelling: Doctor: 'Any swelling that you've noticed?' Patient: 'No.'
Work: 'I've been going to work. I don't know how effective it's been.' Exercise: 'Not as much... I'm not exercising as I would normally.'
To 'persistent cold symptoms or earaches, sore throat, chest cough, shortness of breath, phlegm,' patient answers 'Uh, no.'
To 'Any difficulty swallowing or acid in your throat, or abdominal pain?' patient replies 'No.'
To 'Any change in your bowel habit, diarrhoea, vomiting or blood in the stool?' patient says 'Uh, no.'
To 'Any difficulty passing urine or blood in the urine?' patient answers 'No, that's all fine.'

Neurologic ROS: Doctor asks 'any headaches, blurred vision, tingling, numbness?' Patient: 'Um, no. But it's the sort of headache maybe in just generally feeling a bit crappy,' indicating mild intermittent headaches without vision change, tingling, or numbness.
Past history: Patient states 'Asthma and hay fever if they can help.'

Inhaler use: Patient: 'I've got one of those, um, preventative, I think... I have it. I've been using the everyday for the morning and night.' This describes daily preventer inhaler use morning and night.
Patient: 'I take, um, one of the antihistamines... I get that from, just from the pharmacy,' indicating OTC antihistamines.
Occupation: 'I work for a health technology company actually.' Living situation: 'Just my wife.'

Patient: 'I like, I do quite a lot of walking, and we did, um, quite a lot while we were out in the, on holiday as well... I was in shorts and, and boots,' supporting frequent walking/hiking with shorts and boots.
Alcohol: Doctor asks 'Drink any alcohol?' Patient: 'Sorry, occasionally, that was.'

Summarizes: fatigue and generalized aches for 'definitely the last six weeks' after US travel; transient calf rash in Feb with 'bit of a sore throat' and 'possibly a little bit feverish'; and multiple negatives for respiratory, GI, and GU symptoms as documented.

Doctor: 'a bacterial infection... called lyme disease that you can get a rash like that from a tick bite. So that's something we would do a test for, as well,' indicating concern and need to rule out Lyme.
Asthma stability: Doctor: 'Any flare-ups of your asthma recently?' Patient: 'Uh, no, pretty well, I think.' Hay fever corresponds to allergic rhinitis.

Doctor plans 'some blood tests, checking all the normal things, like liver, kidneys, blood count, etc. But also... a bacterial infection... called lyme disease,' which maps to FBC, U&Es, LFTs, and Lyme serology.
Doctor: 'if that [Lyme test] comes back positive, then there are specific antibiotics that we would give you to treat it,' matching starting appropriate antibiotics if Lyme serology positive.
Doctor: 'if you book that through the support line,' referring to arranging the blood test (phlebotomy) via the support line.
Doctor: 'when you've had the test arrange a follow up about a week after you've had the test done... we can do that over the phone to start with.'
